utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-05-87-A, the Prosecutor versus Nikola Sainovic et al. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, may I please have the appearances of the parties. The Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. NABTI
utterances.text: Najwa Nabti appearing with Barbara Goy, and our case manager, Colin Nawrot, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And now the Defence counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Toma Fila and Mr. Vladimir Petrovic, Defence counsel for Nikola Sainovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Tomislav Visnjic and Peter Robinson for the Defence of General Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Aleksandar Aleksic, Defence for Mr. Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. On behalf of General Lazarevic Defence team, myself, Djuro Cepic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. On behalf of the Sreten Lukic Defence team, I, myself, am Dan Ivetic, and lead counsel Branko Lukic are present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we start, can all the parties hear the proceedings in a language that they understand? Mr. Sainovic, can you follow the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT SAINOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Ojdanic?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT OJDANIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. This Status Conference is called in accordance with Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, which requires a Status Conference to be convened every 120 days during the appeal proceedings to allow any person in custody, pending an appeal, the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. In the present case, the last Status Conference was held on 18th May 2010. Today's Status Conference was scheduled by an order issued on the 23rd August 2010. First, I would like to inquire into the status of the detention conditions and the health situation of the appellants. If you have any concerns in relation to the detention condition or your state of health that cannot be resolved through the standard procedures, I would like you to raise them now. If you wish, this discussion can take place in private session. I see none. Yes. Yes, Mr. Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in a couple of sentences I wanted to inform you of the progress of dental treatment which concerns me. As you know, it was on the 1st of November, 2009, that dental treatment started, and it ended on the 1st of June, 2010. So it almost took a year. And counting from where the problems emerge, it's been two years now. So in two and a half years, we managed to treat two teeth, and we are at a stage now where implants need to be fitted. I would like to raise the following problem here: The specialist implant surgeon suggested that two implants be made over the course of one year. So six months for two implants to be fitted, then six months' break, and then again six months for the fixed dentures to be fitted. This is too long a period, since I've been plagued by toothache all this time. My Defence team has been working on a motion for my provisional release in order for the treatment to be made in my home country. Based on the documentation we have at our disposal now, all the treatment, that's to say the implants, can be fitted in the course of three weeks, and then we would have a three months' break, following which three weeks would be needed to complete the whole treatment. In other words, the dental treatment that could take place in my home country would last six months in total. That's all I have to say. I have no other problems to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that you still asked for the provisional release so that your dental problem could be treated in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The fitting of implants and the entire procedure could be done in six months' time in my country, whereas here it would take one year. But we are still collecting the requisite documentation in order to file our motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much for your information, and I believe that we'll consider your motion at a later stage. Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would start by saying I am yet again addressing you, and thank you for giving me the floor to address you on the issue of my health again. In the previous three Status Conferences, I think I made submissions concerning my health condition that would amount to a novel, so what I would like to ask for now is five to six minutes to address you on the following issues. Let me first inform you that on the 5th of July of this year, surgery was conducted of the thrombosis of my left leg, across its length, and not as some of the medical findings state, that the surgery only involved part of my leg up to the knee. That's incorrect. Number 2, yesterday, in the Royal Hospital of Bronovo, I have been undergoing urinary tract tests. It was a year ago that a diagnosis was already made for this particular condition. The UN Detention Unit physician has ignored this particular condition until yesterday, when the condition became quite critical. I ended up in the hospital yesterday, and the procedure has started. We are yet to see what the outcome will be. Let me say that the physician even went as far as to inform you, in writing, that some of the findings made by the GP were ignored because they weren't thought to be worthy of consideration. And let me say that the GP did not take into consideration some of the specialist's findings. I have this time drawn your attention to two of these problems only in order to demonstrate to everyone in the courtroom that I do not engage in simulating medical conditions. I am not making them up, and nor are any of the specialists in Serbia. Rather, these are medical conditions that have been shown to exist here in the Netherlands. Therefore, I want to highlight the truth and justice, and, on the other hand, I want to draw your attention to the fact that some of the medical staff of the Tribunal have not been fulfilling their duties, have been closing their eyes to the actual situation, and have not been fully informing you, the Appeals Chamber, and all the other interested parties. And let me not go into that issue again, because I've discussed that issue on the previous conferences. Mr. President, I would like to seize this opportunity to thank you personally for your efforts in expediting the procedure leading to my leg surgery. It was a critical point in my medical condition, and absent your support and the support of some other individuals of the Tribunal, I would have found myself in a very difficult position, indeed. Finally, Mr. President, I do continue to have medical problems, and let me tell you, in all honesty, that the problems were not summed up in that one-page document you received on the 13th of September from the UNDU hospital. I do not wish to engage in polemics here, and this is the reason why: The President of the Tribunal, Mr. Robinson, has shown personal interest in assisting my medical condition and health, in keeping with the Rules of the Tribunal. I wish to put you on notice of this, and I wish to thank him for it here. I hope that I've not taken up too much of your time, and thank you for your patience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm very glad to know that the procedure has already started. I believe that, you know, you also have to take care of yourself in the Detention Unit. As for your complaints, I certainly will convey them to the commanding officer of the UNDU as well as to the Registrar. Yes, Mr. -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I just wish to add something for the record to what my client just said. It has to do with yesterday's report of the physician from the UNDU which was made according to your request. I have to note that it's contrary to the previous report to a large degree. The previous report was dated the 19th of July, and it is especially contrary to the findings of Dr. Tan, who is a specialist of implantology and whose reported is dated the 1st of July this year. Yesterday's report mainly states that my client's treatment could have been concluded if he had not insisted on postponing it because he wishes to have it done in his country. However, Dr. Tan's report, dated the 1st of July, states what General Pavkovic already said; namely, that the entire treatment could last up to a year and a half. This is what I wanted to notify you about, and we will submit the request for provisional release in a short time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just wish to use this opportunity and thank you for resolving positively two of my requests for provisional release, and the unfortunate circumstances were such that this happened over a short period of time. Thank you for this, once again, and that will be all for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, as for the provisional release, I would like to inform the parties that in your submissions, you have to show that, you know, the certain treatment is not at all available in the Netherlands and to show us what are the advantages to be treated in Serbia, so that to justify your request for the provisional release, because this Bench has been dealing with the requests for the provisional release for several times already. I do not want to see the repeated submissions. Thank you. Yes, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we requested a provisional release of Mr. Sainovic. For certain reasons you denied that, and there is nothing I have to add about this. But another issue has arisen in the meantime, and I would ask you to resolve it, if possible. If -- you said if treatment in Holland is possible, we do not need to send him to Serbia. I agree with you. However, there are two possibilities. One is to have his healthy teeth pulled out, and I don't think that anyone in the world could request this of any man. If he doesn't want that and if they do not want to pay for treatment for him in the Netherlands, I agree with you that he doesn't have to go to Serbia, where this would be at no cost for this Court, but I cannot understand that someone wants to force him to have his teeth pulled out because that's cheaper. And he has no money to pay this. He has been here for eight years. So this is just one small remark in relation to your decision. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. But I believe that this is an administrative issue, rather than a judicial matter, especially concerning the costs of the treatment, and I still hope that your client will consider the treatment plan offered by the Dutch doctor in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe you didn't understand me. He wants to accept it. This is how I understood that, that you do not want to let him go to Serbia. For me, it's a finished story. But the options that he's being presented with, we cannot force him to have his healthy teeth pulled out because it's cheaper than having his teeth fixed. It's a humanitarian issue. It has to do with the rights of man as well, and that's the essence. It is a judicial issue, because human rights are a judicial issue. I heard that maybe people have their teeth pulled out in Guantanamo Bay, but not here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that, you know, depending on the exact amount that Mr. Sainovic may be required to pay, and he will have the opportunity to seize the Registrar of the Tribunal or eventually the President for the relevant request, explaining why he would not be able to bear the cost himself. I think this is all I have to say at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If there is nothing else, let's record the recent procedural history. Before we turn to any issues that the parties may wish to raise, there remain a few outstanding matters with respect to the briefs and other relevant filings that I would like to address. First, as regards the public redacted version of the briefs, I note that the public redacted version of Mr. Lukic's reply brief has yet to be filed. I would therefore encourage his counsel to do so as soon as possible and to ensure that the paragraph numbers in the redacted version of this filing are the same as in the confidential version of his reply brief. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can report that that has been submitted for filing this morning, so it should already be in the system, working its way through the Registry distribution system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, indeed. Secondly, on the 7th September 2010, the Appeals Chamber granted Professor David Scheffer's application for filing an amicus curiae brief in relation to the mens rea requirement of aiding and abetting, as established by customary international Law. The Prosecution and Mr. Ojdanic were order to file their submissions in response, if any, by 27 September 2010. The Appeals Chamber will consider the parties' submission in those briefs, when addressing their relevant arguments on the merits of the appeal, in the appeal judgement. Third, I have been informed that the translation of the trial judgement into B/C/S is complete and has been filed today. In this context, I recall that the Defence have the opportunity to request the variation of their grounds of appeal, after having read the B/C/S translation of the trial judgement, provided that they show good cause under Rule 108 of the Rules. In this regard, I would strongly encourage parties seeking such variation to do so as soon as possible so that their motions may be decided upon and the supplemental briefing completed, where applicable, before the end of this year. Finally, there is at present one outstanding Prosecution motion filed yesterday. The Prosecution requests that the Appeals Chamber lift the confidentiality of Exhibits 4DA1 through 4DA24. These exhibits were admitted by the Appeals Chamber, pursuant to Rule 115 of the Rules, in its confidential decision of the 12th of February, 2010, which granted, in part, Mr. Pavkovic's motion to admit additional evidence. The Prosecution submits that Mr. Pavkovic's counsel, who originally requested that these exhibits be treated confidentially, has subsequently indicated that those exhibits may be part of the public record. The Prosecution argues that Mr. Pavkovic repeatedly referred to those contents of the Exhibits 4DA1 through 4DA24 in its supplemental brief filed publicly on the 8th March 2010. It further contends that it was informed by counsel for Mr. Pavkovic that it was now acceptable to discuss those exhibits in public. Consequently, the Prosecution submits that those exhibits should be classified as public, since there appears to be no exceptional reason for keeping them confidential. I invite counsel for Mr. Pavkovic, if he is in the position to do so right now, to respond to the Prosecution's motion to which the Prosecution made a reply. Before you start, I just want to know whether you need the private session for further discussions. Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not necessary. Thank you, Your Honour. As my colleague Mr. Ackerman said in the correspondence with our colleagues from the OTP, we have nothing against this, and we agree that these documents may be of a public character. There is no need for them to be kept confidential anymore. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any reply from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. NABTI
utterances.text: No reply. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I shall now determine this matter in my capacity of the Pre-Appeal Judge. I note that there is no objection to the Prosecution's motion to lift the confidentiality of the Exhibits 4DA1 through 4DA24. I also observe that the contents of those exhibits were disclosed in Mr. Pavkovic's supplemental brief which was filed publicly on 8th March 2010. Finally, I recall that all proceedings before the Appeals Chamber shall be public unless there are exceptional reasons for keeping them confidential. In the present instance, I found that no exceptional reason exists to justify the confidential stature of the Exhibits 4DA1 through 4DA24 of the confidential Prosecution's motion to lift the confidentiality of exhibits. For the foregoing reason, I grant the Prosecution's motion and direct that the Registry of the Tribunal to classify as public exhibits 4DA1 through 4DA24 and the confidential Prosecution's motion to lift confidentiality of exhibits. Well, I believe that there are presently no other pending motions before the Appeals Chamber in this case. At this point, I would like to ask the parties whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise at this time. Is there any issues that the Prosecution would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MS. NABTI
utterances.text: There are no issues pending with the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I turn to counsel for Mr. Sainovic. Do you have any other issues you would like to raise, Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the only issue that I would like to raise, and on which I consulted with the other Defence counsel, is the issue of the time-limit within which we will be required to read the trial judgement in order to act in accordance with Rule 108. You rendered a decision on the 29th of June, 2009, stating as much. Upon consultation with the accused and others, we believe that the shortest time-limit that we need is three months. It may seem long, but we have to read through every page of the judgement and we have to see the positions vis-a-vis the other accused. Then we have to check the translation against the original, and we do, indeed, need the time to deal with this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I found that there is no time-limit on this matter in our Rules. But, however, I hope that you could do it as soon as possible, especially within three months. I hope if you have any supplemental briefings which you would like to submit, you'd better do it within that period of time; at least within this year. Is that clear, Mr. Fila? Thank you. And the counsel for Mr. Ojdanic, do you have any other issues to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Your Honour. We join the submission put forward by Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Counsel for Mr. Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have any other submissions than the one put forth by Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel for Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. At this moment, nothing to raise, just to add that we also join to the proposal of Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And the counsel for Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we also acknowledge that Mr. Fila's accurately stated our position jointly on the matter he presented, and we have nothing further to add at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe that this -- yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NABTI
utterances.text: Pardon me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NABTI
utterances.text: If I could just respond to the proposal of the Defence regarding having an additional three months to respond. At present, the Prosecution would agree that 30 days is reasonable to review the judgement in B/C/S with their clients, given the time they've already had to meet with their clients and discuss this matter in preparing their notices of appeal as well as their full briefing. However, if additional time is needed, the Prosecution would request that that be made in writing so that it can respond to the arguments supporting good cause established under the Rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much for your submission. And I believe that, you know, we have an extraordinary case, and the translation of the whole judgement took about 14 months already, and it took me quite a long time to read the whole judgement, trial judgement. And I believe that the Defence counsel will do a lot of checking work in this aspect, so I believe that a longer time is worthy for them to do so. If you insist, you may raise your objections and for the Appeals Chamber to consider. But, however, I think three months' time for any submissions may be reasonable, what I have said. That is, you know, any supplemental briefing should be submitted within this period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NABTI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There is nothing further I have to add at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. By this stage, I have to remind the Prosecution that you have 10 days to respond after the Defence file their submissions for the variation of their briefs, according to the Rules. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: MS. NABTI
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I believe that's all. This concludes today's Status Conference. I thank the parties for their attendance, and the hearing is adjourned.
